liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- Starts with QMS, swaps to the Dead at 0:27, QMS at 0:50, Dead at 1:27, then QMS at 1:59 to the end [1]
- Reviewer found the Dead's Cream Puff War really good [2]
- Reviewer rated QMS's Pride Of Man really good [2]
- Garcia's solo snarls, resembling Clapton's playing of the period, and the whole number drives hard [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Wildflowers - Please Come Home**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Ralph Gleason interviews Jerry Garcia**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **Grateful Dead - Cream Puff War**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **QMS - Pride Of Man**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]
- **QMS & Dead composite - Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [14]

## The recordings

- **gd67-04-08.tv.hanno.12623.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 5 songs; 19 min; rated 4.27/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: Poor sound quality, about what you'd expect from a 1967 recording; The recording has a few dropouts; First track is distorted; overall sound is poor, though acceptable for the era [2][4][7][10]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: announcer's [1]
- The broadcast has an announcer's intro and outro and a 4:30 Ralph Gleason interview with Jerry Garcia [1]
- The announcer's closing remarks say three bands played the same song [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd67-04-08.tv.hanno.12623.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Uli Teute and Hanno Bunjes; source: Soundboard [1]

claims.text: Starts with QMS, swaps to the Dead at 0:27, QMS at 0:50, Dead at 1:27, then QMS at 1:59 to the end
The broadcast has an announcer's intro and outro and a 4:30 Ralph Gleason interview with Jerry Garcia
Poor sound quality, about what you'd expect from a 1967 recording
Reviewer found the Dead's Cream Puff War really good
Reviewer rated QMS's Pride Of Man really good
Garcia's solo snarls, resembling Clapton's playing of the period, and the whole number drives hard
Called the standout of the whole show, despite a few dropouts
The recording has a few dropouts
Reviewer hears Pigpen singing a brief snippet of the Robert Johnson blues
First track is distorted; overall sound is poor, though acceptable for the era
Wildflowers' track has a tight, nice groove
Reviewer finds the sound horrible and wants a better copy
The announcer's closing remarks say three bands played the same song
Reviewer hears the order QMS, Dead, Wildflowers, repeated, then all three bands mixed together to finish
Reviewer says the third vocalist isn't David Freiberg and the solo in the third section isn't Gary or John
Reviewer says the composite actually blends QMS, the Dead and the Wildflowers, as the announcer's outro indicates
Reviewer says Gary Duncan always sang Walkin' Blues with QMS, not Dave Freiberg
